clips.speaker: Melissa Murray
clips.title: NYU法学教授梅丽莎·默里：投票权法案被削弱，少数族裔选区划分面临挑战
title_lines: 少数族裔选区划分面临挑战

subtitles.en: So David you're exactly right that the voting rights act has been under siege for some time this began in 2013 with Shelby County versus holder which eviscerated the pre clearance regime that required states with the history of suppressive voting laws and practices to first clear any changes in their voting laws with the Department of Justice or a three judge court.
subtitles.zh: 大卫，你说得对，投票权法案已受到围攻一段时间。这始于2013年的谢尔比县诉霍尔德案，该案废除了预先批准制度，该制度要求有压制性投票法历史的州在修改投票法前，必须先获得司法部或三人法官小组的批准。

subtitles.en: In the wake of that decision in 2013 states rushed to implement new laws and procedures around voting including more restrictive laws regarding voter ID.
subtitles.zh: 2013年该裁决后，各州匆忙实施新的投票法律和程序，包括更严格的选民身份法。

subtitles.en: This new challenge to section two of the voting rights act really hobbles what was left of the voting rights act in terms of a means of keeping states from promulgating more suppressive voting laws.
subtitles.zh: 对投票权法案第二节的新挑战，严重削弱了该法案剩余部分阻止各州颁布更多压制性投票法的能力。

subtitles.en: It is made it a lot harder for redistricting to happen in a way that maximizes or optimizes the potential of minority groups to elect candidates of their choice.
subtitles.zh: 这使得选区划分更难最大化或优化少数群体选举其选择候选人的潜力。

subtitles.en: And more importantly the court was a little craven and how it decided this on justice Alito did not say he was eliminating or ending section two and said he said he was preserving its central tenants.
subtitles.zh: 更重要的是，法院的裁决有些怯懦。阿利托大法官并未说他要废除第二节，而是说他在保留其核心原则。

subtitles.en: And what that means is while section two will no longer be used to challenge racial gerrymanders that disadvantage voters of color.
subtitles.zh: 这意味着，虽然第二节将不再用于挑战不利于有色人种选民的种族不公正划分选区，

subtitles.en: It still stands unlikely will be able to be used to challenge redistricting efforts in blue states that try to optimize the voting strength of those constituents.
subtitles.zh: 但它仍然不太可能用于挑战蓝州试图优化选民投票力量的选区划分努力。

clips.speaker: Steven Stachinsky
clips.title: 彭博能源主编：中国能源安全布局，战略储备与电动车降低依赖
title_lines: 彭博能源主编 Steven Stachinsky
战略储备与电动车降低依赖

subtitles.en: So, before we let you go, I do want to ask you about China because crude imports fell 20% in April. That's the lowest level since 2022. About half of Chinese supply as you know comes from the Middle East, talk to us a little bit about what China has done to insulate itself from this exact scenario, but it's not a perfect system and how long can they last given the hit to their energy supply.
subtitles.zh: 最后问一下中国：4月原油进口下降20%，为2022年以来最低。中国一半供应来自中东，他们如何应对？能撑多久？

subtitles.en: I think China for much of the last decade has cared so much about energy security and they've they've diversified in so many different ways. I could go, you know, we could talk for an hour, but what they've done, but let's just look at oil, for example, they've actually been increasing their domestic oil production.
subtitles.zh: 过去十年中国高度重视能源安全，多元化布局。以石油为例，他们一直在增加国内产量。

subtitles.en: They're also very strategic with their reserves. A lot of last year, you know, we were talking about run rates being sort of low at Chinese refiners and yet their imports for crude were so high because they were filling up their strategic reserves when oil and Brent was around $60, $70, the Chinese were buying. So they actually have a lot of strategic reserves there as well.
subtitles.zh: 他们战略性地补充储备：去年油价在60-70美元时大量进口，炼厂开工率低但进口高，就是在填充战略储备。

subtitles.en: They've limited the amount of fuel that they're they're also exported, you know, it's been going on and off in the early days of the war that they asked the refiners to kind of cut back on exports there. And at the same time, when you look at their how they consume oil, that's also shifting, you know, it's this is more of a long term story, but you know, the EV boom and the electric truck boom everything in China means that they're going to be depending less and less on that fuel in the future.
subtitles.zh: 他们还限制燃料出口，要求炼厂削减出口。长期看，电动车和电动卡车普及将降低石油依赖。

clips.speaker: Steven Stachinsky
clips.title: 彭博能源主编：中国天然气有压力点，广东地区夏季或现气荒
title_lines: 彭博能源主编 Steven Stachinsky
广东地区夏季或现气荒

subtitles.en: And on the media term, there are some pressure points. And I think one of them still is natural gas, 30% of their LNG came from Qatar last year. And while the country itself also again like oils very insulated, they've got domestic gas supply, they've got inventories, they've also got pipeline imports from Russia.
subtitles.zh: 中期存在压力点，天然气是其中之一。去年中国30%的LNG来自卡塔尔，尽管有国内供应、库存和俄罗斯管道气，但仍有压力。
en_highlights: 30% of their LNG came from Qatar

subtitles.en: The LNG actually does play a somewhat key role in the Guangdong region of China, and that region is basically China's factory. It might not be well known to the rest of the world, but it's basically, it's got the economic power of South Korea.
subtitles.zh: LNG在广东地区扮演关键角色，该地区堪称中国工厂，经济规模相当于韩国。

subtitles.en: It's huge. And because of its location on China's eastern coast, they do import quite a bit of LNG for power production as well as use in pet camps and other industries. And so if it starts to get really hot, for example, this summer, and if there's a draining of hydro facilities, then you could see a crunch in China for gas if they're not able to get what they're getting from the Middle East, likewise also for oil to an extent.
subtitles.zh: 广东沿海大量进口LNG用于发电和工业。如果今夏高温导致水电出力下降，而中东供应受阻，中国可能面临天然气紧张，石油也有类似风险。

clips.speaker: Dr. Carlos Del Rio
clips.title: 埃默里大学专家：病毒传播方式令人关注，密切接触是关键
title_lines: 埃默里大学传染病专家
病毒传播方式令人关注

subtitles.en: No, it actually does. This Andy's antivirus is the only one that's pressed person to person. And there was an outbreak in Argentina in 2018, 2019, where some of the things that you were mentioning actually happened.
subtitles.zh: 不，实际上确实存在。这种病毒是唯一一种通过人际传播的。2018至2019年阿根廷的疫情中，就出现了你提到的类似情况。

subtitles.en: Some person just got infected because they were in the same room with another person that was infected or they were in the same bathroom. It is very clear that if you have very close intimate contact, for example, in this case, the index case, then his wife got infected, they were in the same cabin.
subtitles.zh: 有人仅仅因为与感染者同处一室或共用卫生间就感染了。很明显，如果存在非常密切的接触，比如这起事件中的首发病例，他的妻子在同一船舱内就感染了。

subtitles.en: They could have been intimate sexually. There's a lot of reasons why the wife got infected so quickly and then developed symptoms, but that doesn't mean it's an all or non phenomena.
subtitles.zh: 他们可能有性接触。妻子快速感染并出现症状的原因很多，但这并非绝对现象。

subtitles.en: Clearly, there's a lot of things about the transmission we don't fully understand. And I think this outbreak is going to help us right to understand that it is very clear that the closer you are, the more intimate contact, the more likely you are to get infected.
subtitles.zh: 显然，关于传播我们还有很多未知。这次疫情将帮助我们理解：接触越近、越亲密，感染可能性越大。

subtitles.en: But that doesn't mean that we have not seen what appears to be fairly casual mechanisms of infection.
subtitles.zh: 但这并不意味着我们没有观察到看似相当随意的感染机制。

clips.speaker_context: Distinguished Professor at Emory School of Medicine's Division of Infectious Diseases

clips.speaker: Dr. Carlos Del Rio
clips.title: 埃默里大学专家：世卫组织表现卓越，美国疾控中心能力下降令人痛心
title_lines: 埃默里大学传染病专家
美国疾控中心能力下降令人痛心

subtitles.en: Well, first of all, I want to say that the World Health Organization has really done a remarkable job starting with their director general, Dr. Tedros, and then the rest of the WHO team.
subtitles.zh: 首先，世界卫生组织从总干事谭德塞博士到整个团队，都做得非常出色。

subtitles.en: Maria Vankerhoven and her team, they've done a tremendous job. You know, Dr. Tedros is there and side in Tenerife helping and providing leadership and talking to the Spanish government and ensuring that the boat was able to dock over there in the passengers can be safely and securely disembarked.
subtitles.zh: 玛丽亚·范克尔霍夫和她的团队也做得非常出色。谭德塞博士就在特内里费岛提供领导力，与西班牙政府沟通，确保船只安全靠岸，乘客安全下船。

subtitles.en: I think we have seen a much diminished CDC if you think about a prior outbreak, let's think the outbreak of Ebola. CDC very quickly was involved very CDC very quickly sent a team over there CDC was providing something very important, which is technical assistance.
subtitles.zh: 与之前的埃博拉疫情相比，我们看到疾控中心的能力大幅下降。当时疾控中心迅速介入，派遣团队，提供非常重要的技术支持。

subtitles.en: We're not seeing a lot of technical assistance happening for CDC right now. In fact, it almost seems like the CDC response occurred after many many days. It was almost, you know, too late, too little too late. And that's unfortunate because, you know, we need a strong CDC as American citizens.
subtitles.zh: 现在我们看不到疾控中心提供多少技术支持。实际上，疾控中心的反应似乎滞后了很多天，几乎可以说是太少、太迟。这很不幸，因为作为美国公民，我们需要一个强大的疾控中心。

subtitles.en: We want a strong CDC. You want a CDC that's a leader in global health, not only nationally, but globally. And to see as such a diminished CDC, to me as an infectious disease physician and as a public health expert is actually quite painful.
subtitles.zh: 我们希望疾控中心强大，成为全球健康领域的领导者，不仅在国内，也在全球。看到疾控中心如此衰落，作为传染病医生和公共卫生专家，我感到非常痛心。

clips.speaker_context: Distinguished Professor at Emory School of Medicine's Division of Infectious Diseases

clips.speaker: Dr. Carlos Del Rio
clips.title: 埃默里大学专家：不必波动，但需关注公共卫生基础设施
title_lines: 埃默里大学传染病专家
但需关注公共卫生基础设施

subtitles.en: I think about this one, I would not be worried. I agree with Dr. Tedros. I think there's still a lot of trauma left from COVID.
subtitles.zh: 对于这次疫情，我不担心。我同意谭德塞博士的看法，新冠疫情留下的创伤仍然很多。

subtitles.en: But I would say don't be worried. But this is not the first outbreak. This is not the last outbreak. What I we worried about is that we will continue to see this kind of outbreaks.
subtitles.zh: 但我想说，不必担心。这不是第一次疫情，也不是最后一次。我担心的是我们会继续看到这类疫情。

subtitles.en: We are continuing to have outbreaks like this one. Believe me, a hint of ours in a cruise ship was not in my bigger card of things that was going to happen in a cruise ship. And yet it happened.
subtitles.zh: 我们不断遇到这样的疫情。相信我，游轮上的汉坦病毒并不在我预料之中，但它确实发生了。

subtitles.en: So we're going to see more things like this one. And what people in the US need to be worried about is our public health infrastructure. They need to be worried about we can see the CDC has been significantly diminished and in relevance. And a lot of people have left all the expertise have left CDC.
subtitles.zh: 因此，我们还会看到更多类似事件。美国人需要担心的是我们的公共卫生基础设施。我们看到疾控中心的重要性已大幅下降，许多专家已经离开。

subtitles.en: So I would say that what we need to ask for and what we need to be worried about is the state or public health and global health expertise in our country, rather than this is specific outbreak.
subtitles.zh: 所以我认为，我们需要关注和担忧的是我们国家的公共卫生和全球健康专业能力，而不是这次具体的疫情。

clips.speaker_context: Distinguished Professor at Emory School of Medicine's Division of Infectious Diseases
